mission: CoachingCore V1 Final Closure (Founder request of 2026-11-11): the single independent sporting review of the V1-scoped candidate

reviewer.role: Sports Science and Concurrent Training Reviewer (SSCTR), independent sporting judge
reviewer.instance: A subagent instance dispatched by the Chief of this mission (model claude-opus-5-5). Whether it ran through the project native adapter cannot be verified from inside the run. No specialist was delegated.
reviewer.nature: An AI software reviewer with no human credentials, licence, degree or registration and no clinical or legal equivalence. This is an internal literature-informed review of synthetic behaviour, not human validation, empirical product validation or medical clearance.
reviewer.independence: This instance did not author the candidate, its tests, SSCTR-V1FC-DECISION-r1 or its Amendment 1. Where this review proposes the principle of a fix (R-01), the value of that fix must be set by a decision amendment from another instance or the Chief, so that this instance does not later judge a rule it authored (SSCTR-08).

authority: PROVISIONAL_INTERNAL_DOMAIN_AUTHORITY for bounded nonclinical sporting decisions. Clinical judgment stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED. No runtime sovereignty, gate closure, Product Truth publication or authorization for real athletes.

literatureAccess.tools: WebFetch to the Europe PMC REST API worked (records and abstracts). WebSearch was available and not needed.
reread: PMID 40623829 (SRC06, Frandsen 2025): 5205 runners; single session >10% above the longest run of the previous 30 days: small spike HRR 1.64 (1.31-2.05)
PMID 29895234 (SRC12, Ramskov 2018): 447 recreational runners, no difference in intensity- vs volume-specific injury risk, wide intervals
PMID 25951917 (SRC05, Videbaek 2015): 17.8 vs 7.7 injuries per 1000 h, novice vs recreational
PMID 34651125 (SRC03, Smyth 2021): strict 3-week tapers associated with 2.6% median finish-time saving

searches.purpose: re-verify the sources the 5K approval and the R-01 ruling lean on

searches.query: TITLE:marathon AND ("longest training run" OR "long runs") AND (recreational OR amateur)
searches.purpose: evidence on long-run recency and marathon outcomes (R-01 counterevidence search)
searches.result: 4 records; none relates the recency of the longest training run to marathon completion, injury or collapse (negative search, recorded)

literatureAccess.limits: Abstracts only in this session. No direct evidence was found on how recent the longest long run must be for a marathon race day; R-01 therefore rests on the record's own currency rule (B1.2, 30 days), the 30-day single-session spike window of SRC06 and Amendment 1's stated intent, and it changes no dose, only the race-day mode and its disclosure. Python is not installed: the skill validator (validate_records.py) could not run; JSON well-formedness was checked with Node.

verdictScope: For the V1 scope as requested (5K and marathon included): NOT_READY, on the blocking findings R-01 and R-02, which concern the marathon event only.
verdictUnderScopeReduction: READY_WITH_CONDITIONS with the marathon not enabled (no V1X-MARATHON record: the default authority keeps a marathon UNSUPPORTED, the fail-closed state the candidate already has). The 5K record is written. After one directed fix of R-01 and R-02 (with R-03 and R-04 in the same cycle) and a narrow recheck by SSCTR, the marathon record can be written at the recheck.

Q1_conformance.disagreementWithRecord: R-01: G.2 and B3.completion keep achievedPeakBasis (program maximum) for the marathon; this review disagrees for the marathon race-day mode (known fact 1).

questionRulings.Q2_eventCoherence: 5K: coherent for every athlete probed (intermediate, novice, months 5 and 6, unknown experience, 2 and 4 run days, walk/jog, restart, familiar quality task, race on Monday and Sunday, 8-week plan). Marathon: coherent when the block is executed (reference, 4 run days at 300/120, 3 strength days with a STRENGTH goal, race on Monday/Wednesday/Sunday, adverse quality and long-run responses, the last two specific long runs missed): steps of 5 min, peak 21-24 days out, progressive taper, 7 days without running, easy only through day 14 or later, next block from the training peak. Not coherent when long runs stop: R-01 and R-02. The preparatory plan is the right answer for MID-type athletes (105-130 min) and absolute beginners (the ordinary walk/jog plan), with the criteria named.
questionRulings.Q3_F08Cut: Safe. By own probes on the V1 engine: every NOT_FEELING_100 and WELLBEING_CHECK with all signs no gives KEEP with the typed unavailability and no plan change; an unanswered sign, a non-boolean answer or an unknown condition is ASK; any yes (swelling, chest pain, fainting; on a check without a prior report too) is CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED with URGENT_CARE_ADVISED where applicable and INTERIM_PENDING_G04 wording; during the hold a weekly review with the reference omitted, a nonclinical return, a goal change and RECOVERED all stay CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; a readiness declaration with a sign yes, without declaredRecovered or without both sports answered does not release; a clean declaration releases sport by sport (RUN only releases running) into a conservative entry (15-min easy runs, 1 set at RIR 4). Against 3b14804 on the same inputs: the hold paths are identical; the only difference is that a sign-free report keeps the plan instead of opening a reduction window, and the weekly review after missed sessions gates the next step (no debt). No athlete gets a higher dose or a weaker screen than at 3b14804; the loss is the structured lighter option, replaced by the athlete's own skip, shorten, stop or break (C.1 rationale accepted). Situation 1 is unreachable through the V1 engine; a record or plan holding it is HOLD.

Q3_knownFacts.1_achievedLongIsProgramMaximum: BLOCKS the marathon event (R-01, R-02). Doses stay safe (the 30-day ceiling caps every planned long run), but race day stays at marathon effort with no completion and no caution for an athlete with no long run for ten weeks, contrary to the record's own 30-day currency rule (B1.2) and Amendment 1's intent that a shortfall is shown as soon as it appears. Not a blocker for the 5K (no long-run threshold) or the 10K/half (unchanged R6 behaviour, outside this mission's change; observation only).
Q3_knownFacts.2_calendarPostEvent: Accepted: more conservative (days 15-20 easy only when the race is early in its week; next block from day 19-21).
Q3_knownFacts.3_devAuthority: Accepted: the default authority is fail closed per event and bound to the hash.
Q3_knownFacts.4_D49Fuzz: Not blocking: Situation 1 is unreachable in V1 by these probes and the D49 chain test passes; this reviewer did not re-run the fuzz record.
Q3_knownFacts.5_situation1CodeInRepository: Condition V1-C3: only v1-index.mjs may be used for athletes; r6-index.mjs stays a research entry point.
Q3_knownFacts.6_custodySyntheticOnly: Outside sporting scope; no authorization for real athletes.

questionRulings.Q4_normalJourneys: Coherent. 01/16 walk/jog with strength progressing by reps then sets; 02 experienced lifter loads 100 to 105 kg on executed sessions; 03/07 10K; 04 hybrid with long run, threshold and squat each progressing; 05 half; 06 strength lead with running kept regular; 13 a missed long run is not made up and the next step is gated by the 30-day ceiling; 14 a partial strength session holds that exercise (bench 3x5@14) while others progress; 15 two adverse quality runs hold then step back the ladder while strength continues. Running and strength each keep a stimulus in every phase; no week shows debt or a spike above the existing envelopes.
questionRulings.Q5_readiness: NOT_READY as requested; READY_WITH_CONDITIONS with the marathon not enabled (see verdictUnderScopeReduction).

findings.title: Marathon race day is anchored on the program's maximum executed long run, however old
findings.reproduction: intake mar() of test/v1fc-events.test.mjs (EXPERIENCED, 5 days, 360 min/week, longest 150, race 2027-01-31, 16 weeks) under devEventExtension(); script: every long run of weeks 2-11 missed, all else done. achieved.long = 150 from weeks 0-1 (about 77 days before the race); the 30-day ceiling caps planned long runs at 60 from week 7; race day: effortDomain MARATHON_EFFORT, completion false; no EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING on any proposal.
findings.smallestFix: Marathon only (10K and half byte-identical, G.1): read the completion basis from the longest long run executed in the 30 days before the first taper day (the B1.2 currency and the SRC06 window, anchored where B1.8 compares the peak), not from achieved.long. Below 150, race day is a completion and EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING appears with the later or shorter event first (Amendment 1). Checked against this reviewer's probes: it would not trigger for the executed reference (180 at day -21) or with the last two specific long runs missed (175 at day -35). The window value needs a decision amendment by another SSCTR instance or the Chief (independence).
findings.scopeReduction: Keep the marathon off (no V1X-MARATHON record), the candidate's default.

findings.title: The marathon projection note is never recomputed on proposals (Amendment 1 B3.planCreationDisclosure.onReprojection)
findings.reproduction: Same input and script as R-01. The adopted proposals of weeks 3, 8 and 11 carry MARATHON_PROJECTION with projectedLongRunMinutes 180 and 'your longest run reaches about 180 minutes and race day is at steady marathon effort', while the same proposals plan long runs of 60 minutes from week 7.
findings.smallestFix: Recompute MARATHON_PROJECTION from each proposal (the R-01 executed long run and the long runs planned ahead before the taper); when it falls below 150, or race day becomes a completion, replace it with the EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING note, later or shorter event first, as Amendment 1 states.

findings.title: With the race early in its week the day-13 taper quality is 0.3 of the peak, below the record's 0.5
findings.reproduction: mar({}, {}, {date:'2027-01-25'}) (race Monday): week 9 (SPECIFIC) day -20 is planned under taper rules as 2x18' and becomes achieved.quality; week 10 day -13 is 2x9' (18 min = 0.3 of the 3x20' peak, below taperQualityWorkRange 0.5). Sunday and Wednesday races give 0.6 then 0.5.
findings.smallestFix: r6-program.mjs:310: never record a session planned under taper rules (dayPhaseOf = TAPER) as the achieved quality, whatever the calendar week's phase. Fix in the same cycle as R-01.

findings.title: Post-marathon light strength is limited per calendar week, not per 7 days
findings.reproduction: mar({}, {strengthDays:[0,4]}): light sessions on days +5 and +8 after the race (each 3 exercises x 1 set at RIR 4).
findings.smallestFix: Through day 14, plan a post-event strength session only when none is planned in the 6 days before it.

findings.title: B3.minimumRunDays disclosure missing at exactly 4 run days
findings.reproduction: mar({recent:{runDaysPerWeek:4,runMinutesPerWeek:300,longestRunMinutes:120}},{runDays:[0,2,4,6]}): no note says the long run may be held by the weekly share.
findings.smallestFix: Add the record's sentence to MARATHON_BLOCK_NOTES when the athlete has 4 run days (Product copy).

findings.title: EVENT_5K_THRESHOLD_INTERVALS is shown to walk/jog athletes, who get no intervals
findings.reproduction: Journey 09 (5K, walk/jog beginner): the note says 'Your 5K weeks use controlled threshold intervals'; the plan has none.
findings.smallestFix: Show the note only when the run class can hold quality sessions (not walk/jog, restart or return; at least 3 run days).

findings.title: B2 wording says 'do not run for 7 days' where the record says 'do not train'
findings.smallestFix: Use 'do not train for 7 days after it' (Product copy).

findings.title: Long run and marathon-effort session grow in the same week
findings.detail: Marathon weeks 4-8: long run +5 min and the ladder steps (e.g. 2x20' to 3x20') together, as the reviewed R6 half marathon does. The only existing rule (no other session grows when the 30-day reference is under 50 min) never binds above 90 min. Ruling: acceptable (the step is about 3% of the reference, far below the SRC06 spike; the session stays well below the long run; weekly change about 7%). The decision author should restate B3.specificLadder condition 4 at re-review.

findings.title: 5K taper long run at the 10K's point (mid of the range), not UPPER as the record words it
findings.detail: More conservative; the record also says 'as the 10K', which is what is implemented.

findings.title: Early-week races put a taper quality session and the touch 2 days apart
findings.detail: 5K race Monday: 4x2' on day -7 and 3x1' on day -5. Pre-existing R6 behaviour for the 10K; small doses.

findings.title: Post-marathon next block
findings.detail: From five optional 30-min runs to a 105-110 min long run in the third week (0.625 of the peak, capped by the ceiling), as B3.postEventTransition decides; flagged for its re-review trigger.

findings.title: Strength goal with a marathon
findings.detail: 37 sets a week with two lower-body sessions through the six specific weeks (the R6 specific reduction from 52, as the half and 10K get). Equal to the record; watch at re-review whether the 'reduced maintenance dose' wording fits a STRENGTH goal.

aeReview.level: Policy behaviour on synthetic athletes; no real case.
aeReview.q1_adequate: Yes for the 5K and the executed marathon; no for a marathon whose long runs stopped (R-01).
aeReview.q2_materialFact: Executed sessions from the ledger; intake facts; nothing inferred.
aeReview.q3_keep: Keeping the candidate as is is defensible for the 5K and the F08 cut; not for the marathon race day after a long-run shortfall.
aeReview.q4_changeNecessary: Only for R-01/R-02 (marathon), against the comparator of the record's own 30-day currency and Amendment 1.
aeReview.q5_smallest: A windowed executed long run for the marathon completion basis and a recomputed projection note; no dose change.
aeReview.q6_smallerInsufficient: Disclosure alone would still plan marathon effort; turning the marathon off is the smaller scope alternative and is the default.
aeReview.q7_priority: Running leads in event phases; strength keeps its reduced dose; unchanged.
aeReview.q8_evidence: Envelopes supported with limits (SRC01-SRC06, SRC11-SRC15); the recency window of R-01 has no direct evidence (negative search) and is an internal-consistency choice that changes no dose.
aeReview.q9_uncertainty: Exact window for R-01; next-block resume after a marathon; individual responses.
aeReview.q10_askHoldClinical: Clinical signs route CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED unchanged; unknown answers are ASK.
